layer9_head0: Head Name: Synaptic and Neuronal Projection Specificity Explanation: This head captures gene expression patterns strongly enriched in excitatory and inhibitory neurons, especially cortical layer 5-6 excitatory neurons, SV2C- and VIP-expressing interneurons, and SST-expressing interneurons, as indicated by high coefficients in synapse and neuron projection GO terms. The elevated scores highlight synaptic and vesicle-related genes that distinguish mature neuronal subtypes from glial cells, reflecting their specialized roles in neurotransmission and neural circuit integration.
layer9_head1: Head Name: Neuronal Projection and Synapse Markers Explanation: This head captures gene expression programs related to neuron projection and synaptic functions, strongly highlighting excitatory neurons and specific interneuron subtypes (e.g., cortical layer 5-6 excitatory neurons, SV2C- and VIP-expressing interneurons, and SST-expressing interneurons) with the highest coefficients in GO terms for neuron projection and synapse. These patterns distinguish neuronal cells by their elevated expression of genes involved in neuron projection development and synaptic organization, unlike glial cells which have lower coefficients in these features.
layer9_head2: Head Name: Metabolic and Ion Transport Regulation Explanation: This head captures gene expression programs related to metabolic processes and ion transport, with the strongest emphasis in microglial cells and SV2C-expressing interneurons, reflecting their high metabolic activity and specialized ion channel functions. The elevated coefficients in microglia align with their active role in metabolism and immune responses in the CNS, while interneurons’ strong association with ion transport and synaptic regulation reflects their critical role in neuronal signaling.
layer9_head3: Head Name: Synaptic and Neuronal Projection Regulation Explanation: This head captures gene expression patterns related to synapse formation, neuron projection, and ion transport, which are strongly elevated in excitatory and inhibitory neurons—especially cortical layer 5-6 excitatory neurons, PVALB-, SST-, VIP-expressing interneurons, and cortical layer 4 excitatory neurons. These features reflect molecular processes underlying synaptic signaling and neuronal connectivity that distinguish mature neuronal subtypes from glial and immune cells in the CNS.
layer9_head4: Head Name: Neuronal Synaptic and Vesicle Transport Explanation: This head captures gene expression features related to synapse formation, neuron projection, and vesicle-mediated transport, showing strongest relevance in excitatory neurons and interneurons (especially cortical layers and PVALB-, SV2C-, SST-expressing interneurons). The enrichment for synaptic and vesicle-related GO terms reflects the specialized roles of these neuronal subtypes in neurotransmission, distinguishing them from glial and other non-neuronal CNS cells.
layer9_head5: Head Name: Ion Transport and Synaptic Function Explanation: This head highlights genes and biological processes related to ion transport and synaptic activity, with stronger emphasis in interneurons (especially SST-, PVALB-, and SV2C-expressing) and excitatory neurons of cortical layers 2–6, consistent with their roles in fast neurotransmission and electrical signaling. It also distinguishes microglial and phagocyte populations by lower association with these neuronal functions, reflecting their non-neuronal, immune-related roles in CNS homeostasis.
layer9_head6:
Head Name: Synaptic and Neuronal Projection Specialization  
Explanation: This head strongly emphasizes genes involved in synapse formation and neuron projection, with highest coefficients in cortical and interneuron subtypes, especially SST-, VIP-, and PVALB-expressing interneurons and cortical layer neurons. The pattern reflects enhanced expression of synaptic and projection-related genes distinguishing excitatory and inhibitory neurons from glial cells, consistent with their specialized roles in neurotransmission and neural circuit connectivity.
layer9_head7: Head Name: Neuronal Synaptic and Projection Features Explanation: This head captures gene expression patterns related to neuronal components such as synapse formation and neuron projection, with the strongest coefficients in cortical layer 5-6 excitatory neurons, SV2C-expressing interneurons, SST- and PVALB-expressing interneurons, and other neuronal subtypes, reflecting high expression of synaptic and projection-associated genes. Non-neuronal glial and immune cells have consistently lower values, indicating this head distinguishes neuronal cell types by their enriched synaptic and projection machinery.
layer10_head0: Head Name: Neuronal Projection and Synaptic Function Explanation: This head distinctly highlights genes and biological processes related to neuron projection and synapse organization, showing the strongest positive coefficients in cortical layer 2-3 and 5-6 excitatory neurons, SST- and PVALB-expressing interneurons, and SV2C-expressing interneurons. These patterns reflect the specialized role of excitatory and inhibitory neurons in forming complex synaptic networks and neural circuitry, while glial and immune-related cells have consistently lower coefficients for these features, indicating this head captures neuron-specific connectivity and synaptic activity.
layer10_head1:
Head Name: Neuronal Projection and Synapse Regulation  
Explanation: This head captures gene expression programs related to neuronal projection, synapse formation, and membrane protein complexes, which are most strongly expressed in inhibitory interneurons (SV2C-, VIP-, PVALB-, and SST-expressing interneurons) and excitatory cortical neurons, reflecting their specialized roles in synaptic connectivity and signal transmission. The enhanced coefficients for GO terms involving neuron projection and synapse specifically distinguish mature neuronal populations, consistent with their complex morphology and communication functions in the CNS.
layer10_head2: Head Name: Neuronal Projection and Synapse Regulation Explanation: This head captures gene expression patterns related to neuron projection, synapse formation, and molecular function regulation, most strongly distinguishing cortical excitatory neurons and interneurons by their elevated scores in GOCC neuron projection and synapse terms. The high coefficients for these features in excitatory neurons (e.g., layer 2-3 and layer 5-6) and interneurons reflect their specialized roles in forming and modulating synaptic connections within the central nervous system.
layer10_head3: Head Name: Neuronal Projection and Synapse Development Explanation: This attention head captures gene expression patterns related to neuron projection and synapse formation, showing the highest importance in excitatory neurons (especially cortical layers 4 and 5-6) and interneurons such as SST- and VIP-expressing cells. It highlights features involved in neuronal connectivity and signaling, which are key for distinguishing mature neuronal subtypes from glial cells and immune-related phenotypes.
layer10_head4:
Head Name: Neuronal Synaptic and Ion Transport Regulation  
Explanation: This head captures gene expression patterns related to synapse structure, neuron projection, and ion transport, which are most strongly pronounced in excitatory and inhibitory neurons (e.g., cortical layer 2-3, layer 5-6 excitatory neurons, SST-, VIP-, and PVALB-expressing interneurons). It distinctly highlights neuronal cell types by emphasizing molecular functions and biological processes involved in synaptic signaling and ion channel activity central to neuronal communication.
layer10_head5: Head Name: Synaptic and Neuronal Projection Development Explanation: This head captures gene expression patterns related to synapse formation and neuron projection that strongly distinguish excitatory and inhibitory neurons, especially cortical layer 5-6 excitatory neurons, SV2C-expressing interneurons, and SST-expressing interneurons, which exhibit high coefficients for GOCC synapse and neuron projection terms. The head reflects biological processes essential for neuronal connectivity and signaling, with lower relevance in glial and immune cell types.
layer10_head6:
Head Name: Synaptic and Neuronal Projection Activity  
Explanation: This head captures gene expression patterns related to synapse structure and neuron projection, strongly distinguishing excitatory and inhibitory neurons—especially cortical layer 5-6 excitatory neurons, SST- and VIP-expressing interneurons, and mixed excitatory neurons—by highlighting their enhanced synaptic machinery and projection-related genes compared to glial cells. It reflects key neuronal functions such as neurotransmission and connectivity that are less prominent in oligodendrocytes, astrocytes, and microglia.
layer10_head7: Head Name: Neuronal Projection and Synapse Regulation Explanation: This head captures gene expression programs related to synapse formation and neuron projection, strongly distinguishing excitatory neurons and interneurons by elevated coefficients in GO terms like “GOCC synapse” and “GOCC neuron projection.” The head also highlights increased emphasis on ion transport and cell signaling processes, consistent with the high functional demand for synaptic communication and neuronal connectivity in cortical and GABAergic neurons compared to glial cells.
layer11_head0: Head Name: Ion Transport and Synaptic Function Explanation: This head strongly emphasizes genes involved in ion transport and synaptic processes, particularly highlighting excitatory neurons (cortical layers 4, 5–6, 2–3) and interneurons (SV2C-, SST-, VIP-, PVALB-expressing) that exhibit high coefficients for ion transmembrane transport and synapse-related functions. These features reflect the critical roles of ion channel activity and synaptic transmission in neuronal signaling, distinguishing neurons from glial and immune cell types in the CNS.
layer11_head1: Head Name: Neuronal Synaptic Function Explanation: This head emphasizes genes involved in synaptic structure and neuron projection, strongly distinguishing excitatory neurons and interneurons by high enrichment of synapse-related pathways (e.g., GOCC synapse and neuron projection). It captures the prominent expression of synaptic and vesicle-mediated transport genes in cortical neurons compared to glial cells, reflecting the specialized cellular machinery for neurotransmission in these central nervous system populations.
layer11_head2: Head Name: Neuron Projection and Synapse Coordination Explanation: This head captures gene expression programs strongly enriched for neuronal projection and synapse-related functions, such as "GOCC neuron projection" and "GOCC synapse," which show the highest coefficients in excitatory neuron subtypes and interneurons, especially cortical layer 2-3 and layer 5-6 excitatory neurons as well as SST- and VIP-expressing interneurons. These terms reflect the complex morphology and signaling of mature neuronal cells, distinguishing them clearly from glial lineages like oligodendrocytes and microglia that have lower values in these features.
layer11_head3: Head Name: Synapse and Neuron Projection Regulation Explanation: This head captures gene sets related to synaptic structure, neuron projection, and intracellular transport that are strongly elevated in excitatory neurons and interneurons, particularly cortical layer 5-6 excitatory neurons, SST-, VIP-, and PVALB-expressing interneurons. The high weighting of synapse organization and vesicle-mediated transport terms reflects key functional specializations of mature neurons, distinguishing them from glial cells such as oligodendrocytes and microglia that show lower values.
layer11_head4: Head Name: Neuronal Synaptic and Projection Activity Explanation: This head emphasizes gene sets related to synapse, neuron projection, and neurogenesis, which show the highest coefficients in excitatory neurons (especially mixed excitatory, cortical layer 2-3, and layer 4 excitatory neurons) and interneurons (notably SST- and VIP-expressing subtypes). These patterns reflect the distinct high expression of synaptic and projection-related genes in neurons versus glial cells, capturing neuronal specialization in connectivity and signaling within the central nervous system.
layer11_head5: Head Name: Neuronal Synaptic and Projection Genes Explanation: This head distinctly captures gene sets related to synapse formation, neuron projection, and molecular function regulation, most strongly characterizing excitatory neurons of cortical layers 5-6 and 2-3 as well as interneurons like SV2C-, VIP-, PVALB-, and SST-expressing types, reflecting their high expression of synaptic and projection-related genes. The elevated coefficients for GO terms such as neuron projection, synapse, and molecular function regulator correspond to known molecular specializations of neuronal subtypes compared to glial cells and microglia.
layer11_head6:
Head Name: Synapse and Neuron Projection Specialization  
Explanation: This head captures gene expression programs related to synaptic function and neuron projection, showing the strongest coefficients in mature excitatory and inhibitory neurons, particularly cortical layer 2-3 and layer 5-6 excitatory neurons and SST- and PVALB-expressing interneurons. These patterns reflect the high expression of synaptic vesicle, neuronal projection, and membrane-associated genes that define neuronal identity and connectivity within the central nervous system.
layer11_head7:
Head Name: Ion Transport and Neuronal Projection Regulation  
Explanation: This head primarily captures gene expression programs related to ion transport and neuronal projection, which are highly pronounced in excitatory and inhibitory neurons (especially cortical layers 4-6 excitatory neurons and various interneuron subtypes). It reflects the biological specialization of neurons in maintaining electrochemical gradients and complex cellular projections, distinguishing them from glial and immune-related cell types such as microglia and oligodendrocytes.
